summary: Torkel Brekke is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied under Jens Braarvig and Georg von Simson at the University of Oslo and under Richard Gombrich at Oxford. He held posts at PRIO, Oslo Metropolitan University, and MF Norwegian School.

Torsten Wiesel studied at the Karolinska Institute (c. 1947–1954). He taught Francisco Varela and held appointments at Johns Hopkins University (c. 1955–1959), Harvard University (c. 1959–1983), and Rockefeller University (1983–1998).

Toru Haneda was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Sinology, and history. Educated at the Third Higher School, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University, he served extensively as a professor, director, and dean at Kyoto University, and chaired Toho Gakkai.
Toru Kumoi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Center for Open Humanities Data and as a senior researcher at the Humanities Information Studies Institute (attested 2015).

Toru Sagara was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji and later held academic positions at Ibaraki University (c. 1952–1968), the University of Tokyo (c. 1968–1982), and Kyoritsu Women's University.

Toru Takahashi was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Keijo Imperial University (1926–1940), Dongguk University, Fukuoka University, and Tenri University (1950–1964).

Toru Tomabechi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University and the University of Lausanne, he held posts at Lausanne, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and the Center for Open Humanities Data.
Toshiaki Yamada is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He completed his studies at Toyo University (c. 1966–1974) and subsequently held an academic post there from around 1985 to 2017.

Toshifumi Goto is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his PhD at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann and studied under several scholars, later holding professorships at Osaka University and Tohoku University.

Toshihiko Izutsu was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies who studied and long taught at Keio University. He also held posts at the East Asia Institute, Kaikyoken Kenkyujo, McGill University, and the Iranian Institute of Philosophy.

Toshihiko Kimura is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Tohoku University. He later held posts as a lecturer at Tohoku University, associate professor at Tokai Gakuin University, and professor emeritus at International Buddhist University.
Toshihiro Wada is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied under Vashishtha Narayan Jha in 1981 and served as a professor at Nagoya University from around 1989 to 2020.

Toshiichi Endo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under Mahinda Palihawadana and W. S. Karunatillake, later teaching at the University of Hong Kong.

Toshikazu Watanabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held appointments at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia, and Kokugakuin University, where he was a professor in 2018.

Toshiki Osada is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. After studying at Hokkaido University, he held posts at Kyoto University of the Arts (c. 1994–2003) and the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (c. 2003–2019).

Toshinori Ochiai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held posts as professor at Kacho Junior College, library director at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and director of the Institute for the Study of Ancient Manuscript Buddhist Canons.
Toshio Ando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from around 1931 to 1934. He held academic posts at Doho University and Otani University (c. 1952–1973).

Toshio Horiuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (c. 2002–2008) and held research positions at Toyo University (c. 2014) and Zhejiang University (c. 2018).

Toshio Nagahiro was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as a professor and researcher, and later became president of Kyoto Tachibana University.

Toshio Sako is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima and Jikido Takasaki, and completed doctoral studies at Columbia University under the supervision of Alex Wayman.
